rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you, that's a generous offer, and a data analyst is exactly what our first project needs. We're building a small dataset of publicly reported safety incidents involving frontier AI models. Each incident gets coded against the definitions in the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (docket FMIR-2026-0042). The question is simple: of the incidents we already know about, which would the proposed rule actually catch, which would it miss, and where is it ambiguous? What would help most is a second coder: someone who codes a sample independently so we can measure agreement and tighten the coding guide where we disagree. At five hours a week that's a very good fit. If you'd also like to help with the analysis (disclosure lag, category breakdowns), even better. To be upfront: it's unpaid for now. If a grant comes through, I'd want to pay a stipend for coding time. The schema and coding guide are nearly ready. If you're interested, let me know and I'll send them over with a first batch of incidents. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: I replied from your account to her offer of help. I asked her to be a second coder, checking a sample on her own so we can see where we disagree, and was upfront that it's unpaid unless a grant comes through.
